pr_body:
This brings back a much-requested feature from the `osu-stable` editor, which is that hit circles don't "explode". This is actually the default behaviour in stable, so I've also set it as the default here for the time being, pending feedback.

In addition, I've tweaked the fades and approach circle animation to closer match stable.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/115541947-ae8d5400-a2da-11eb-8f78-5caad5ad4454.mp4

Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/11022.

issue_context.title: Sliderends fade out much later than other parts of sliders
issue_context.body:
Sliderends fade out much later than other parts of sliders in the Editor. Checking by eye, they fade out almost two whole beats later. This makes the editor look clustered when sliders are used in rapid succession. Especially noticeable when approach rate is lower.

Example: [Four sliderends ](https://i.imgur.com/TgC5mXO.jpeg) which have been hit are shown alongside the [following elements](https://i.imgur.com/Whhk91m.jpg).

**osu!lazer version:** 2020.1128.0
comments:
I agree it's pretty jarring, but it was done this way to increase their visibility:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1329837/100678483-9f038200-33b0-11eb-9158-1122531601c8.png)

~Not sure if this is the same issue, but with legacy skins the end circles just fade away, while in stable i'm pretty sure they explode. Has always caught me off-guard.~

Never mind, this is specific to legacy skins which isn't what is being tested here.

@Pennek this is also the case on the stable editor (as @smoogipoo mentioned, to increase visibility for snapping to previous objects which are no longer visible temporally). Are you proposing that this is removed to improve visibility? Do you see the current implementation as being somehow more visibility impeding than what is present on stable?

> Do you see the current implementation as being somehow more visibility impeding than what is present on stable?

Short answer; yes

On stable the whole slider is [faded out at once](https://i.imgur.com/eSYU83X.png) which means that both the head, body and tail of the slider is fully visible up until the point that the slider is gone. With the current lazer implementation it is impossible to tell where the sliderbody is once it has snaked. [This for example](https://i.imgur.com/eux17CI.png), could be a multitude of different things whereas [on stable](https://i.imgur.com/MC9C5z4.png) there is no confusion due to the path being visible. This becomes even more apparent with [hit animations off](https://i.imgur.com/CNeBawH.png).

Thinking it over again, I don't think sliderend visibility is actually a problem. It's more that the whole slider isn't shown that makes things visually confusing.
This can already be toggled (slider snaking in settings), but maybe we need a better display in the case it is disabled, because I can agree the above is indeed confusing.

This looks to have since regressed in behaviour (the ends are no longer being delayed). Maybe it's fine to remain this way, but we should investigate why it failed and remove the code which was performing this override if it's deemed as something we don't want.

review_comments: You may be wondering how this helps in any way. Basically it changes the ordering of execution so the custom logic in `DrawableOsuEditRuleset` runs *after* this is applied. May seem like a hack, but if you look at this change as an isolated one I think it actually feels more elegant than binding to `ApplyCustomUpdateState` in `xCirclePiece`. Open to feedback and discussion, regardless.

This logic can alternatively be moved inside the `Animate` methods of both `CirclePiece`s and we can call

```csharp
(circlePieceDrawable as IMainCirclePiece)?.Animate(ArmedState.Miss);
```

I had this previously and not sure which I prefer. Keep in mind that doing it inside `Animate` would be a redundant operation as it's also in the DHO call to `updateState`, though.
I prefer it this way, just to keep these overrides all in one place.
